rows.abstract: Any provision of law to the contrary notwitstanding hospital expenses of indigent patients admitted and confined in private hospitals and clinics under emergency cases shall be subsidized by the government. > Any person who shall avail of the financial assistance granted under this Act shall apply for an indigent identification card with the Department of Social Welfare and Development upon submission of proof of indigency as provided under Section 1 hereof.> The hospital concerned shall transmit monthly billings to the Department of Health of the total emergency admission fee extended to emergency patients under this Act which shall include the relevant information regarding the patient and the facilities extended.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 63, TITLE II OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes that present laws on marriage be amended to allow the innocent spouse who have been granted a decree of legal separation to initiate the necessary petition before the proper courts to finally terminate their marriage and to re-marry, after the lapse of five (5) years from the date of the issuance of the decree. During the hearing, it is necessary that the following elements be properly established: (1) That the petitioner be the innocent spouse; (2) That a period of five (5)years have elapsed from the time the decree of legal separation became final and executory; and (3) Reconciliation between the spouses is no longer possible.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2002-04-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR KILLING, WOUNDING, CAPTURING OR TAKING AWAY OF THE EAGLE AND/OR DESTROYING ITS HABITAT, DISTURBING OR TAKING AWAY OF THE BIRD'S NEST OR EGGS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION FIVE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-ONEHUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Philippine Eagle is a symbol of all life in the rain forest. Just as this bird depends on the rain forests to survice, the earth's survival likewise lies on the preservation of the forests. If the eagle disappears, it means the support forest has disappeared. The survival of the eagle means the survival of our race.  > Following is the proposed AMENDMENT to Section 5, RA No. 6147: "SEC. 5. Any person violating any provision of this Act shall be punished by a penalty of [prision correccional] PRISION MAYOR or by a fine of not less than [six hundred][(P600. 00)] TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00) nor more than (One) FIFTEEN THOUSAND PESOS [(P1,000.00) (P15,000.00), or by both such imprisonment and fine at the discretion of the coourt. In case of any subsequent offense, the Court shall impose both the imprisonment and the fine. In case of insolvency , the corresponding subsidiary imprisonment shall be imposed upon the offender."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2002-04-22

rows.abstract: "Philippine Citizenship Retention Law of 2002." This bill provides that --- "No Filipino citizen who has voluntarily sought or opted to be naturalized in a foreign country shall be deemed to have lost his/her Philippine citizenship. It shall likewise not be lost merely by operation of the law of another country, whereby citizenship of that country is conferred ib that person, unless, by their free, willful and voluntary act, they become a candidate or was elected to any public office in his/heradopted country."

rows.abstract: The provision of any law, rule or regulation to the contrary notwithstanding , the penalty of reclusion perpetua instead of the death penalty, shall henceforth be imposed in cases where the law prescribes the imposition of the death for the violation of its provisions. > Any person who shall be sentenced by final judgment to reclusion perpetua by virtue of this Act shall serve it for the rest of his natural life, without entitlement to any allowance for good conduct, special time allowance forloyalty, or parole save only as the President of the Philippines may allow in the exercise his power to grant reprieves, commutation of sentence or pardon under the Constitution.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05114

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN AND CREATING THE BARANGAY YOUTH COUNCIL IN LIEU THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) is the primary target of any local official seeking a higher post. These traditional politicians spread venom, and the youth comprising the SK become contaminated. Their innocense is lost, and is replaces bythe practices of old, which are the same practices we have repeatedly rejected. > The question now is how do we protect the youth? The solution is quite simple. First, the SK must be abolished. The wisdom in this lies in the fact that the SK has become both a tool and a vehicle for the proliferation of corruption. Cut of this avenue, and we cut off the deadly tentacles of the umprincipled politician.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A HIGHER STANDARD OF PROMOTION AND PROTECTION OF THE RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF FILIPINO OVERSEAS SEAFARERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Overseas Seafarers Act." Rationale: Prevailing state of things and available data attest that the Philippines is among the top, if not the No. 1, source of maritime labor in the world. As a matter of fact the Philippines is regarded as the "manningcapital of the world". Many of the vessels sailing in the world's oceans and seas are now manned by Filipino seafarers who, through the years, have established a reputation as seafarers who are at par or even more competent and reliable compared with seafarers from any other coutnry in the world. > Given the volume of Filipino overseas seafarers and their considerable annial dollar earnings (about $1.5 billion annually) which help sustain the country's economy and growth, the need to come up wiith a definitive policy legislation that will foster the benefits, rights and protection of seafarers has become more pressing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2002-04-23

rows.abstract: This bill aims to propose a system of tracking and monitoring the circulation of all stolen goods and properties in any given locality. It seeks the cooperation and participation of the police in listing and recording all complaints concerning all stolen goods, articles, items or objects within an immediate are or vicinity. Important information must be included and circulated and posted in all pawnshops, thrift shops or in any establishment engaged in the buying and selling of used and secon-hand articles.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY POPULARIZATION PROGRAM THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF SCIENCE CENTERS THROUGHOUT THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Science Centers Act of 2002". This bill intends to strengthen the science and technology popularization program by enhancing the development of regional and provincial science centers. These will serve as the local centers for community science andtechnology education, information and communication among the youth and general population. It shall have the major compoments: (1) Youth Development; (2) Science Communication Outreach; (3) Continuing Research and Development Program (R&D); (4) Interactive Exhibits Development Program; (5) Science and Tecnology for the Masses; (6) Support for the Existing and Establishemt of New Science Centers; (7) External-intern al Linkage and Networking Program; and (8) Manpower Capability Building Program

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442), AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, BY DELETING ARTICLE 130 AND 131 THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: Articles 130 and 131 of the Labor Code of the Philippines refer to NIGHTWORK PROHIBITIONS AND EXCEPTIONS regarding women workers. > Mor eeffective utilization of potential woman force in the developing countries like the Philippines necessitates increasing women's work-participat ion rates and channeling female labor into genuinely productive tasks. Hence, if the nightwork prohibition provisions still in effect, untowards result would prejudice women workers. Therefore, Article 130 and 131 of the Labor Code of the Philippines should be deleted.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2002-04-23

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THAT ALL LIQUOR BOTTLES CARRY A WARNING ON THE BOTTLE ITSELF OR ON THE LABEL THAT ALCOHOL DURING PREGNANCY IS HAZARDOUS TO THE LIFE AND HEALTH OF THE UNBORN CHILD
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is an established and undisputed fact that taking or consuming alcohol during pregnancy causes harmful effects on the unborn child. These  harmful effects of the child include the following: (1) head face deformities; (2) major organ system malfunctions resulting in heart defects, ear infections hearing loss and the like; (3) central-nervous system dysfunctions causing mental retardation and hyperactivity; and (4) arrested growth both before and after birth. > In a country with ahigh birthrate, it is wise that a law be enacted to provide information on the effect of alcohol consumption to the unborn child. This bill seeks to require all liwuor bottles to carry a warning that alcohol intake during preganancy is hazardous to llife and health of the unborn.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2002-04-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SPECIAL HEALTH FOR ALL FUND TO BE USED BY THE LOCAL HEALTH BOARDS FOR THE IMPROVEMENT OF HEALTH CARE SERVICES IN THEIR RESPECTIVE LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The proposed SPECIAL HEALTH FOR ALL FUND shall be used excluding for the following: (1) Upgrading of facilities and equipment of local hospitals, rural health clinics, lying-in clinics, emergency hospitals, puericulture centers, nursing homes, hospices and such other health institutions found in the local areas; (2) Hiring, training and/or continuing education of health workers, caregivers, volunteer health workers and other ancillary personnel employed by the local governments in their healthinstitutions; (3) Building of new health institutions, such as secondary hospitals, specialty clinics or care centers in the local areas; (4) Purchase of needed medicines and medical supplies at the lowest costs in accordance with law; and (5) Establlishment of mobile emergency lifelines or quick-response medical and paramedical teams to respond to disasters, emergencies and other life-threatenin g situations in the community.
